title: Dynamic IO Profiles & Streaming Minimums: Horizon Field Experiment
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Run a timeboxed field experiment to test per-customer dynamic IO profiles (variable input:output weighting) combined with per-session streaming minimums that adapt to workload patterns. Objective is to find a pricing shape that better matches cost-to-serve for very skewed workloads (e.g., embedding-heavy ingestion vs. long-form output generation) while minimizing churn for small/PLG customers and preserving enterprise contract simplicity.

Motivation and background: Current hosted pricing uses a static ingress/egress token split and blunt streaming minimums that misprice many customers: embedding pipelines generate large ingress token volumes with low compute per token; conversely, document generation produces relatively few ingress tokens but heavy egress. We need a way to price closer to marginal cost without creating confusing line items or large bill volatility for end customers. This experiment explores dynamic IO profiles that classify workload patterns and apply tailored input/output unit weights plus a session-aware streaming minimum that declines over the session lifetime (grace curve).

Hypotheses: 
1) Dynamic IO profiles will increase revenue per equivalent compute by ~8-12% from previously underpriced embedding-heavy customers while keeping churn under 1.5% in the pilot cohort.
2) Session-aware streaming minimums (declining grace credits over first N minutes) will reduce billing disputes and improve perceived fairness vs a flat streaming floor.
3) For enterprise customers under contract, applying dynamic profiles as an opt-in addendum will not materially affect renewals if surfaced clearly in the SQ and contract language.

Experiment design: 
- Cohort selection: 500 customers segmented into three buckets: (A) embedding-heavy (top 15% ingress/egress ratio), (B) balanced, (C) output-heavy (long-form generation). Include both PLG and sales-assisted customers; exclude current committed Reserved Capacity customers.
- Treatments: control (current pricing) vs variant 1 (dynamic IO profile applied, streaming minimum unchanged) vs variant 2 (dynamic IO profile + session-aware streaming minimum).
- Duration: 8 weeks active test, 2-week observation window afterward.
- Success metrics: net revenue delta, average bill volatility (std dev week-over-week), number of billing disputes opened, churn rate at 30d post-experiment, NPS micro-survey on perceived fairness.

Measurement plan & telemetry: 
- New analytic events: pricing_applied_variant, session_grace_used, billing_dispute_created, io_profile_assigned, effective_token_weight(input), effective_token_weight(output).
- Primary dashboards: revenue_by_variant, disputes_trend_by_variant, churn_by_variant, avg_bill_stddev_by_customer_bucket.
- Baseline collection: capture 4 weeks pre-experiment of token ingress/egress distributions per customer to seed profile assignment.

Pricing logic (implementation notes): 
- IO profiles are algorithmically selected from a small catalog: EMBEDDING_BIAS (higher ingress weight discount), BALANCED (1:1 baseline), OUTPUT_BIAS (higher egress weight). Weights are multiplicative modifiers applied to the per-token base unit. 
- Session-aware streaming minimums: on session start we provision X credits equal to base_floor, then apply exponential decay over first 20 minutes (configurable alpha) so long sessions pay progressively lower incremental overhead after the warm-up period.
- Billing clarity: invoices will show a single line "Effective token units" and a breakdown modal in Console that expands to show assigned profile and the session grace credit used. No new top-level SKU to reduce procurement friction.

Customer communication & enterprise contract handling: 
- For PLG customers in the cohort we will display an in-console experiment banner with a short FAQ and link to a bill estimator. 
- For enterprise customers with active SOW/commits, apply experiment only as opt-in via an addendum workflow. Legal/RevOps will review addendum language; updates to the enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) will explicitly call out that pricing changes do not alter data routing, storage, or encryption.
- Engage Solutions Engineering for any customers flagged as "high-risk" (> $50k MoM) prior to experiment.

Risk & guardrails: 
- Immediate opt-out threshold: if more than 0.8% of variant customers file billing disputes within week 1, rollback variant for affected accounts.
- Revenue guardrail: reserve ability to cap extra invoice delta per customer at +20% for the experiment period.
- Monitoring: daily alert to PM/RevOps on disputes and unexpected invoice deltas.

Operational deliverables: 
- Confluence experiment spec (link below) with math worksheets for unit economics and example invoices.
- SDK/Backend flags: feature flag pricing.dynamic_io_profiles and pricing.streaming_session_grace.
- Data team: SQL queries for cohort assignment and weekly aggregation.
- Console: estimator UI + invoice breakdown modal.

Approvals required: Finance sign-off on unit economics, Legal on enterprise addendum, Security on SQ language, Eng for runtime telemetry and invoice generation.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment implementation gated behind feature flags and validates on test accounts
Telemetry events emitted for every priced request and aggregated into weekly dashboards
Billing pipeline can cap experimental invoice deltas per customer
Legal review completed and enterprise addendum template available
Data team has provided pre-experiment baselines and cohort assignment output
rollout_plan: Week 0: Baseline data collection and cohort selection
Week 1: Canary on 20 customers (manual validation), legal/finance sign-offs
Week 2-9: Main experiment (500 customers) with daily monitoring
Week 10-11: Post-run analysis and decision: rollback, refine, or scale
